strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real limitations of existing feed-forward methods (fixed input views) and per-scene optimization (computational cost), with clear applications to robotics and real-time systems

Comprehensive system design integrating multiple well-justified components: 3D-annotation-free training framework, novel view selection based on coverage masks, instance-guided contrastive learning with O(NpK) complexity vs O(N²p), and geometry-semantic hierarchical sparsification recognizing differing spatial density requirements

Strong experimental validation showing consistent improvements across sparse to dense views (2-32) with stable performance, ~200× speedup over per-scene optimization (5sec vs 10+ min), and better semantic accuracy than optimization-based baselines
Valuable InstanceMV-14K dataset contribution with 15M+ images and instance masks from diverse sources, addressing the lack of large-scale multi-view semantic data
Practical efficiency focus demonstrated by meaningful memory/computation reductions (2.6M vs 6.4M embeddings) through geometry-semantic sparsification while maintaining quality
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: directly inherits VGGT architecture, uses standard projection-based novel view selection, applies prior voxel-based sparsification [10,17], and makes straightforward adaptations of contrastive learning; contribution is primarily in system engineering rather than algorithmic innovation

Heavy VGGT dependency creates circular reasoning: quality bounded by VGGT, and '3D-annotation-free' claim is misleading as it shifts annotation to VGGT's training; no ablation comparing VGGT pseudo-labels versus alternative supervision or quantifying data contribution vs method improvement

Narrow evaluation scope: restricted to indoor scenes (ScanNet/ScanNet++) with no outdoor or diverse environment testing; semantic evaluation limited to pre-annotated mIoU/mAcc metrics without evaluating truly open-vocabulary queries; promised robotic navigation/manipulation applications not validated; 3D editing shown only qualitatively

Insufficient technical justification for key design choices: 3D feature aggregation via voxel-based CLIP averaging (Eq. 5-6) lacks justification; covariance fusion via moment-matching + isotropic approximation (Eq. 11-12) has no comparison to alternatives; coverage threshold τ sensitivity and MLP architecture in Eq. 5 not discussed; instance mask sampling strategy (Eq. 6) lacks clarity

Evaluation setup concerns: baselines designed for 2-view inputs; extending to multi-view via DUSt3R may not be entirely fair; dense-view comparison (Table 2) uses 16/32 views inconsistently with feed-forward comparisons spanning 2-32 views; ablations (Table 3) only on ScanNet++, missing ScanNet validation

Dataset construction transparency issues: SAM2 used for unlabeled data masks without quality analysis or impact assessment; reproduction instructions for InstanceMV-14K not clearly specified; unclear how to obtain RealEstate10K subset used

Incomplete ablations: missing studies on coverage threshold τ sensitivity, FLEG performance with/without InstanceMV-14K dataset, semantic Gaussian count necessity analysis, and failure mode characterization

Reproducibility concerns: many hyperparameters (voxel sizes εgeo/εsem, coverage threshold τ, MLP architecture) incompletely specified; no code or dataset release mentioned; training details for InstanceMV-14K construction lacking

Generalization and scalability: limited evidence for cross-dataset generalization; 1B parameter model raises scalability questions; no evaluation on challenging scenarios (extreme poses, specular surfaces, outdoor scenes); semantic embedding consistency across views not analyzed
Presentation gaps: Figure 2 overly complex; geometry-semantic density trade-off in sparsification not explicitly discussed; no user studies validating semantic query quality

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical limitations of prior feed-forward methods (fixed views, pose requirements); supports flexible 2-32+ input views without pose.
Key insight on semantic sparsity: DGLE module achieves 95% storage reduction (18.04 MB vs 491.3 MB) while maintaining comparable semantic fidelity, with clear validation in Appendix C.
Technically sound dual-branch distillation framework with novel-view-based supervision to prevent overfitting; instance-guided contrastive learning is computationally efficient (O(N_p K) vs O(N_p²)).

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple views (2-32), datasets (ScanNet++, ScanNet, Replica), metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, mIoU, mAcc); consistent improvements over baselines (mIoU 46.61 vs 39.54 at 2 views).
Training without 3D annotations or semantic labels; uses readily-available 2D instance masks from SAM2; enables scalable training on video sequences.
Multi-task capabilities (novel-view synthesis, open-vocabulary query, 3D editing) in single model with clear qualitative improvements (Figs. 3-4).
Well-written, clearly structured paper with thorough ablation studies (Table 3) validating each component and cross-dataset generalization on Replica.
weaknesses: Strictly limited to indoor scenes (ScanNet++, ScanNet, Replica); no outdoor evaluation undermines generalization claims and severely limits real-world applicability.
Performance ceiling bounded by VGGT; Table 4 shows FLEG achieves only 0.681 AUC@15 vs VGGT's 0.668 at 32 views—geometric accuracy cannot exceed distillation source, a fundamental limitation.

Limited component novelty: individual techniques are standard (VGGT distillation from prior work, CLIP features, instance contrastive learning); primary contribution is DGLE module and novel-view selection, which are incremental.

Questionable experimental setup: LSM and Uni3R evaluated using two-view pretrained models selecting nearest views to target, handicapping methods not designed for sparse multi-view settings; subset evaluation for 32-view optimization baselines (Table 2).
Semantic sparsity assumption appears data-dependent; v_sem=0.016 choice is empirically tuned (Appendix C); unclear how the 5% storage claim generalizes to other domains or semantic distributions.
Many hyperparameters (η₁, η₂, λ₁₋₄, τ, voxel sizes) with no sensitivity analysis or cross-validation methodology described; robustness unclear.
GPU memory constraints unresolved—while storage reduced, handling hundreds/thousands of views still limited; no runtime comparisons with baselines provided.
Incomplete semantic evaluation: mIoU/mAcc only evaluate segmentation, not semantic quality; no perceptual evaluation, user studies, or analysis of failure modes on complex multi-semantic scenes.

Missing analysis: no discussion of failure cases, when semantic sparsity breaks down, or why FLEG outperforms baselines beyond sparsity; isotropic Gaussian approximation (Eq. 11) justified mainly by convenience.
Technical clarity issues: MLP architecture for L_feat (Eq. 5) unspecified; 3D feature aggregation module mentioned but not formally defined; notation Π in Eq. 1 could be clearer.
